about: Perfection is a three-row template built from X-Men: First Class: on the right, Michael Fassbender as Erik Lehnsherr stands in a dark room looking at someone offscreen, his face softening from cold scrutiny to quiet admiration across the three shots, and the white column on the left holds what he is being shown. Each row has a subtitle line. He rejects two versions of something, insisting on "the real" one, and the final option, often surprising or obscure, earns his satisfied "Perfection."
origin: The scene is from X-Men: First Class (2011). Erik tells Raven, who has been hiding her blue mutant form, that he prefers "the real Raven" and calls her natural appearance "Perfection." That dialogue became the template's script.
usage:
The template has six boxes in three rows. The large left boxes (1, 3, 5) are the things being shown to Erik; the small subtitle boxes on the right (2, 4, 6) are his lines. A standard run is: option one, "I prefer the real X."; option two, "I said, the real X."; final option, "Perfection."

The joke depends on the third choice. Go deeper into obscurity (the original before the remake), backwards in time (an older version), or toward something weird that still technically counts. Film recasts, game versions, phone models, fonts and food work well.
ideas: I prefer the real Darth Vader.
I said, the real Darth Vader.
